summary: This guide outlines risk mitigation strategies for energy companies facing space weather threats such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections, developed by Dr. Jackson Emery and meteorologist Claire Hansen. It covers monitoring and alerts, infrastructure hardening, redundancy and fail-safes, workforce training, diversification, collaboration and standards, and R&D, with dated company examples. It argues that a severe storm is inevitable and preparedness is key to resilience.
one_line: A strategic guide by Dr. Jackson Emery and Claire Hansen on how energy companies can reduce space weather risks to the grid.
key_facts: Dr. Jackson Emery and meteorologist Claire Hansen developed comprehensive risk mitigation strategies for energy companies facing space weather.
On September 10, 2023, a significant solar event caused widespread service disturbances.
A University of Colorado study predicted that a storm similar to the 1859 Carrington Event could inflict upwards of $1 trillion in damages today.
On December 14, 2023, a timely alert from NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) let Pacific Grid Co. brace for impact and prevent major outages on the U.S. west coast.
Global Energy Inc. retrofitted its transformers across Europe with GIC-blocking technology in early 2024 and reported a 75% decrease in GIC-related disruptions.
In March 2024, TechWave Energy and GridDefence Labs formed a joint venture to develop superconductive materials that reduce vulnerability to space weather.
On September 20, 2023, NY State Electric & Gas activated backup substations ahead of predicted solar storms, preserving power for essential services when two primary substations were impacted.
The Mid-Western Power Alliance championed regular testing and updating of fail-safe mechanisms such as automated switchgears after a minor geomagnetic storm on November 3, 2023.
Energy Texas ran space weather response simulations in late September 2023 and credited them for efficiently managing a grid irregularity two months later.
Wind and solar farms may be less impacted by GICs than nuclear or coal-fired plants, supporting diversification of generation.
The Global Energy Network launched an initiative on February 11, 2024 to create a shared space weather response protocol.
HelioTech Research and Stanford University announced a collaboration on October 5, 2023 to improve predictive analytics for space weather effects on energy grids.
Underground cabling is recommended for new installations because it is less susceptible to space weather than overhead lines.
